text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Homelessness among unemployed youth growing at alarming pace, youth housing organisation says.
- Prime minister Paavo Lipponen said he was unaware of his Social Democratic Party's secret organisation which spied on communists into the 1970s.
- Western reports of Christianity's strong come-back in Russia exaggerated, Finnish study shows. @
- Heavy snowfall during the weekend caused accidents and disrupted traffic in the central parts of Finland.
- Membership of the Freemasons may prevent a judge from hearing a case in which one of the parties is a fellow mason, says Parliamentary Ombudsman Lauri Lehtimaja.
- Finnish animal protection groups want "Flipper" taken off television.
- Finnish national ice-hockey team won four-national friendly tournament, beating Sweden 6-2 in Helsinki on Sunday. @
KAUPPALEHTI
- Finns have invested a record 5.7 billion markka in foreign shares this year, according to the central bank.
- Finnish forestry firms selling off employee housing.

- State indebtedness declining even more quickly than in late summer, Prime Minister Lipponen said. At present rate, state net borrowing will be about 40 billion markka in 1996 vs. earlier estimate of 45 billion.
AMMULEHTI
- Closer cooperation with NATO demands that Finns understand the language of command, says defence force chief. @
- Markka's link to European Exchange Rate Mechanism more significant as a symbol of economic stability than as a change in foreign exchange system, Bank of Finland economist says.
DEMARI
- Social Democratic Labour Minister Liisa Jaakonsaari rejects criticism of union federation SAK, and says job creation now more important than income security.
- Social Democratic Party parliamentary group chairman Erkki Tuomioja says government's proposed reform of regional administration is half-baked and raises many questions. @
TURUN SANOMAT
- Prime Minister Lipponen sees no reason why National Board of Taxation chief Jukka Tammi should step aside during inquiry into tax affairs of company part-owned by Tammi.
- Satellite navigation system helps logging trucks find way on remote forest roads.
